import numpy as np

# Fixed `included` list: every repository whose final AI label is `included`.
included_ids = wlab.loc[wlab["ai_label_final"] == "included", "repo_id"].sort_values().to_numpy()
print(f"fixed included list : {len(included_ids)} repositories")

# Repositories with no event on any day never appear in the activity table, so we cannot
# build the daily matrix from `pilot_weekly` alone: that would drop both the zero days and
# the included repositories that had no activity the whole week.
inc = pilot_weekly.loc[pilot_weekly["repo_id"].isin(included_ids)].copy()
inc["event_day"] = inc["event_date"].dt.normalize()

# The observation window is the full seven requested UTC days, not only the days that happen
# to have events. Re-index to every requested day and to the full fixed list, so days and
# repositories with no observed activity are kept as 0 instead of being dropped.
requested_days = pd.to_datetime(coverage["requested_days"], utc=True).normalize()
inc_daily = (
    inc.groupby(["event_day", "repo_id"])["event_count"].sum()
    .unstack(fill_value=0)
    .reindex(index=requested_days, columns=included_ids, fill_value=0)
    .fillna(0)
    .astype(int)
)
inc_daily.index = inc_daily.index.date

print(f"window days shown   : {len(inc_daily)} (expected 27)")
print(f"included total events this week: {int(inc_daily.to_numpy().sum())}")
print()
print("daily events per included repo (0 = no event observed on a fully-covered UTC day):")
print(inc_daily.to_string())

if not inc_daily.empty:
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))
    inc_daily.plot(ax=ax, marker="o")
    ax.set_xlabel("UTC date")
    ax.set_ylabel("events")
    ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    ax.set_title(
        f"Included repos daily events over the full 27-day calendar window "
        f"(n={len(included_ids)}, 2024 fixed cohort; individual lines, not a cohort-age curve)"
    )
    ax.get_legend().remove()  # 200 entries would cover the chart
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(FIG_DIR / "weekly_included_repos_daily.png", dpi=150)
    plt.close("all")
